key_insight: Broad-spectrum infrared imaging combined with deep-learning translation could provide a radiation-free way to generate radiograph-like views for pediatric skeletal triage.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could reduce reliance on ionizing X-rays in children while preserving a fast, portable screening pathway for musculoskeletal trauma.
method: Review of five IR windows: NIR-I, NIR-II, SWIR, MIR/LWIR, and THz
Uses dual-geometry capture (transmission and reflection) to leverage tissue depth and biochemical contrast
Applies cross-modal AI models and feature-matching tools such as Pix2Pix, CycleGAN, Swin-Unet, SuperPoint, SuperGlue, ALIKED, and LightGlue
evidence_signal: The paper is a narrative review grounded in prior IR biology and cross-modal imaging work, but the abstract does not report new patient-level performance data.
watch_item: Main implementation risks include the need for paired IR/X-ray datasets, regulatory clearance for AI medical devices, and generalization across skin tone and body habitus.
paper_title: Infrared Imaging Empowered by Artificial Intelligence for Pediatric Skeletal Triage: A Narrative Review and Future Perspectives
